A.why: Basalt bodice over a stair-stepped slab skirt with grey bottom tiers: reads as a plinth or cake from above; the sleeves are broad blocks.
A.fix: Replace the stepped slabs with 2-3 angled bell panels from the hip; slim the sleeves; add one bold magma seam.

B.why: All pale ash grey: visible at night, but off-palette and close to the linen and classic families; the ziggurat skirt reads as stairs; the sleeves are broad.
B.fix: Make basalt black the main mass with ash as an accent; use taller flare panels; make the red cracks bold.

C.why: The only true A-line or bell skirt, with a glowing red hem; elegant, but nearly all black, so it fades from above; the sleeves are still full-width.
C.fix: Slim the sleeves and remove the shoulder ridges; add an ash-grey bodice or sash and a magma seam running up the skirt.

D.why: Strongest top-down read and most on-zone (basalt with magma bands), but the many even red-edged tiers read as a pagoda or lampshade; broad sleeves; heavy on parts.
D.fix: Cut to 3-4 varied tiers with crack-like red gaps; slim the sleeves; give the bodice a shapelier neckline.

E.why: A straight black column skirt with no flare; reads as a cassock or coat; vanishes into the dark; the red and gold accents are only hairlines.
E.fix: Build a real bell from the hip; add ash and magma masses; slim the sleeves.

F.why: Open front panels show the legs, so it reads as a coat or tabard; nearly all black; broad sleeves.
F.fix: Close the panels into a continuous bell; fill the gaps with a glowing magma underskirt; add a waist sash; slim the sleeves.

notes: No candidate slims the sleeves: all six keep shoulder-width arm blocks, the same flaw as the earlier gowns. C has the best dress silhouette and D has the best zone read and visibility; C's skirt combined with D's magma banding and a lighter ash accent would be the target. Most sets are too uniformly black for the night camera.
